question: In one study of top-league penalties, goalkeepers dived to a side 94% of the time. Which choice saved most often?
answer: Staying in the centre. Bar-Eli and colleagues found that keepers who stayed put stopped about a third of the kicks they faced, against about 13% for those who dived. Kickers aimed at the middle nearly a third of the time. A goal conceded while standing still looks like doing nothing, so keepers dive.
move: When doing nothing is the best option, it still has to be chosen.
ask: Where is doing nothing my best option, and have I the nerve to choose it?
trap: Diving looks like effort, and effort feels like the best chance.

diagram.caption: Keepers dived 94% of the time, yet staying put saved over twice as often.

source: Bar-Eli et al., J Economic Psychology, 2007
reference: Bar-Eli, Azar, Ritov, Keidar-Levin & Schein, Action bias among elite soccer goalkeepers: The case of penalty kicks, Journal of Economic Psychology, 2007
